titulo: Info Matrix (Textos 08) — Bônus — Gilgamesh e Protagonista

linhas.en:
Another name for Gilgamesh.
Not as in a "#RUBS           Hero King#RUBEking who is a hero#REND,"
but with the implication of being a "#RUBS        King of Heroes#RUBEking over heroes#REND."

The story of Gilgamesh, mankind's oldest hero, was
replicated in the myths of countries all around the world.
The origin of all myths, the model heroes are based on……
referring to him as such would not be an exaggeration.

Heroes of the various mythologies were all more or less
derived from the legend of Gilgamesh.
As such, Gilgamesh possesses the prototypes of the
Noble Phantasms those heroes carry; the original treasures
from before each of their legends were arranged.
Perhaps it's a paradox: unless Gilgamesh owns the original,
it cannot be passed down as a Noble Phantasm
to the heroes that were later derived from him.


             ◆

It was a time when humanity was still few in number.
Ruling his kingdom and living in luxury as he saw fit, 
gathering all the treasures of the world into his treasury.

In that treasury held the originals
of treasured swords that saved later heroes,
and cursed swords that took the lives of heroes.

Herein lies the reason Gilgamesh is the King of Heroes.
Ordinarily, a hero would only have a single Noble Phantasm.
Owning unlimited numbers of them would naturally include
the "legend" those heroes are weak against.
It would be impossible for the average Heroic Spirit
to contend with him.

As a Heroic Spirit, he is absolutely indomitable
in battle against other Heroic Spirits.
There may be a number of heroes who hold the title of king,
such as the King of Knights and the King of Conquerors,
but there is only #RUBS              under heaven and earth#RUBEone man in the world#REND with the name
of "the absolute king of all heroes."
キーワード１偽名テキスト

As a young man, Gilgamesh's violent disposition only grew.
Naturally, the people of Uruk, but even the gods
who dispatched him were greatly perplexed by his violence.

"Gilgamesh is not fulfilling his original purpose."
"That insolent creature needs someone to punish him―――"

With that conclusion, the gods sent a single being
to the surface. Their name was Enkidu.
Made by a god and given her blood, just like Gilgamesh.

             ◆

They had neither #RUBSgender#RUBEsex#REND nor a fixed form.
Shaped from clay by a god, Enkidu was "Uruk's greatest
weapon," able to change their shape at will.

According to that#RUBS  mother's#RUBE god's#REND will,
Enkidu confronted Gilgamesh before the Temple of Uruk.
Clashing like a storm, they fought throughout the city.

After a fierce battle, they both collapsed to the ground,
praised each other's valor, and became peerless friends.

For Gilgamesh, who'd been without equal, it was
the first time he found someone he could call "a friend."

             ◆

Afterwards, though his egotism didn't change, Gilgamesh
was admonished by Enkidu and softened his tyranny.

Gilgamesh, who had someone who understood him in Enkidu,
defeated the forest guardian and beast of a god,
Humbaba, and took possession of every treasure as
the greatest king on Earth.

At that time, Gilgamesh was so dazzlingly powerful,
he was an existence that not even the gods could
avert their eyes from.

A goddess fell in love with that Gilgamesh.
It was the goddess of fertility, Ishtar.
She proposed to Gilgamesh, but he quickly refused.
He knew that how much Ishtar was
a whimsical and brutal witch who broke men.

Ishtar, enraged by Gilgamesh's insult, begged her father,
Anu, in tears for retribution and released the greatest
of Divine Beasts, "the Bull of Heaven" onto the earth.

#RUBS The Bull of Heaven#RUBE"Gugalanna#REND" was #RUBS   a skyscraping#RUBEan extreme#REND disaster clad in storms.
When it appeared, a seven-year famine and destruction
struck the earth. In other words, the downfall of Uruk.

Against this unrivaled Divine Beast, Gilgamesh and Enkidu
worked together to fight it and repelled it splendidly.
The goddess had lost face once again.
Naturally, Isthar's rage hadn't calmed, so she requested
of the gods the death for either of the two.
For a mortal to kill the beast of the gods was a sin.

Ishtar's wish was granted, and one of the two,
Enkidu, created by the gods and unable to defy that decree,
slowly weakened and died.

……the sole person who understood that king, Enkidu.
Just how large a shadow this loss cast over Gilgamesh
is told in the rest of his life afterward.

             ◆

Enkidu was an autonomous weapon made from clay by the gods.
In SE.RA.PH terms, they'd be something like an AI.
Being complete from birth, they neither grow nor evolve.
Able to take various forms as needed, it's said their
usual form was of a 16-year-old, with long hair shining
a faint light-green, unable to be taken as a boy or a girl.
キーワード２偽名テキスト

Gilgamesh's final Noble Phantasm, exemplifying creation―――
the beginning of everything.

Bearing the name of a god from Mesopotamian mythology,
causing the severance of space, the Sword of Rupture, Ea.

The god Ea is believed to be the quasi-deification of the
power of the planet that turned, smashed, and stabilized
the surface of the Earth in its primordial stages,
covered in gas and seas of magma.

Most gods began building nations after primordial Earth
stabilized into a world that could sustain life,
but Ea was a god who built the planet before them.

Gilgamesh's sword, bearing Ea's name,
alters space itself by agitating spacetime through
the rotation of three gigantic layers of force fields.

Its true power is not something to be used against
a single lifeform, but against the world. Even among
the many Noble Phantasms possessed by Servants,
it's one of the best; the sword "that cut the world apart."

A measure of the divine attributes in someone's body.

Though he possesses the highest of Divine Spirit aptitude,
Gilgamesh himself hates the gods so its rank has decreased.
スキル１偽名テキスト

Not the golden ratio of one's body,
but how much money one is destined to acquire in life.

At Rank A, it could be described as a soul of gold.
Even while living the high life in a Goldie manner,
he won't ever want for money in his life.
スキル２偽名テキスト

The ability to acquire higher quality items.
It's good luck for frequently obtaining even rare items,
but since it only applies to Gilgamesh himself,
it does not benefit his Master.

             ◆

Gilgamesh is a collector of treasures.
"I've collected all the treasures of the earth"
is what Gilgamesh likes to say, but it's not a metaphor.
He collected, stored, and sealed away a sample of
all the technology developed during his age.

Rather than just treasure, what Gilgamesh stored away
was "the essence of human ingenuity" itself.
If it's not in his treasury, then it's something made
"by a new humanity, through an entirely new concept"
or "by intelligent life from another celestial body";
one of the two.

So of course he has airplanes and submarines.
Human desires haven't changed#RUBS                Anno Domini, The Christian Era   #RUBE from before AD#REND, and arts
from the age of magic weren't inferior to modern technology.
People usually realize the "tools of hope" they dream of,
and each time, it ended up confiscated by the king's hand.

The attack skill Gilgamesh uses, "Gate of Babylon,"
ejects the treasure he's collected like arrows.
The gates to the golden capital open, and his treasures
are shot out from his treasury.

As a side note, after the Noble Phantasms shot out are used,
they return to his treasury no matter how far they went.
"Hmph. I have a Noble Phantasm that excels at retrieval,"
says the person himself.
スキル３偽名テキスト

The demigod king who governed the Sumerian city-state Uruk
in a time before Christ. Not as a mere legend but having
truly existed, the king accounted in mankind's oldest epic,
"The Epic of Gilgamesh."

With great Divinity as 2/3rds god and 1/3rd human,
he was perfected as a transcendent being who attained
everything in the world, without equal in the world.

As a child, he was adored by people as the ideal ruler, but
perhaps from being seen as almighty, he grew inconsiderate
of his subjects and he came to rule Uruk with an iron fist.

However, simple despotism doesn't make him a tyrant;
Uruk truly prospered, he found a friend he could talk to,
and personally subjugated monsters that threatened
his people, are heroic qualities that cannot be questioned.

He is the heroic figure who defeated the bull so large
it blocked out the heavens, and rendered the civilization of 
his fortified Sumerian city unshakeable.

             ◆

The following is historical fact, not from "The Epic."
According to a piece of inscription found in an excavation
of its ruins, Uruk was a city-state on the Persian Gulf in
Southern Mesopotamia, him as 5th king of its 1st dynasty.
It gained assets from sea trade and conquered Southern
Mesopotamia. He prevailed against Aga, king of the Kish,
who ruled the north and unified the city-states of Sumer.
However, due to reckless deforestation to build ships,
their agricultural land was devastated.

That's why Gilgamesh went all the way to far-off Phoenicia
(modern Lebanon) seeking giant trees, the Cedar of Lebanon,
fought against the resident of the woods, Humbaba,
won, and said to have brought back many trees with him.
設定１偽名テキスト

According to "The Epic," after the loss of Enkidu,
Gilgamesh fell into depression, his previous vigor gone.

Gilgamesh was shocked by the fact that Enkidu,
whose strength had not been inferior to his own, could die.

Tormented by anxiety over "death," he finally decided
to set off for the underworld in search of immortality.

It was said there was once a sage who'd survived by putting
many animals on an ark before a deluge assailed the Earth.

This sage was said to be the only one on Earth
to escape from death and live on to the present.
Seeking him, Gilgamesh set off to the wilderness alone.

At the end of that long journey, through many hardships,
Gilgamesh finally arrived at the underworld.
There, he met the sage named Utnapishtim, spoke with him,
and finally obtained the Herb of Immortality.

Gilgamesh was to transcend the "death" that had
taken even Enkidu.

             ◆

His heart's desire fulfilled, on his way back to Uruk,
Gilgamesh stopped by a spring. He cleansed himself;
apparently intending to test it in perfect condition.

However.
As he was bathing, a hungry snake
happened to smell the Herb of Immortality.

By the time he noticed, it was too late.
When Gilgamesh emerged from the spring in a panic,
all that remained was the skin that snake had shed.

Having lost the Herb of Immortality,
Gilgamesh was irritated for a long time,
but he made his way back to his castle in Uruk.

After this, while strict, he ruled his state quietly,
entrusted it to the next king and went to his eternal rest.

Without telling anyone the Herb of Immortality's location.

             ◆

Mankind's oldest King of Heroes, Gilgamesh.
Discord with the gods, the quest for immortality,
a deluge that enveloped the world.
In that epic was the basis of every legend.

The truth of this epic, with many of its finer details
uncertain, now lies across the veil of romance.

As another side note, the reason snakes are reborn with
a new body every time it sheds its skin is because it
stole and ate Gilgamesh's herb…… or so they say.
Apparently, the way snakes live appeared to the ancients
as a kind of immortality that was unavailable to humans.
